title: bug: the scheduler package-boundary scan throws on a regex literal inside a template expression, and the throw blinds the rest of the walk
description:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-08 21:12Z by worker-bcaa6d5e, foreground, no lease (single test file):

  pnpm exec vitest run packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts
  Tests  1 failed | 55 passed (56)   EXIT 1
  > keeps scheduler registrars behind the package-root import boundary
  Error: boundary scan failed for apps\daemon\src\deployment\deploy-candidate-environment.ts: Error: unterminated quoted source token

THE NAMED DAEMON FILE IS NOT THE DEFECT. `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-environment.ts:74` is valid TypeScript:
  .map(([name, value]) => `${name}='${value.replace(/'/gu, "'\\''")}'\n`)

THE DEFECT IS IN THE SCANNER. `packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts:99` `templateExpressionEnd()` — the brace matcher that finds the end of a `${...}` — has branches for `'`, `"`, nested backticks, `//` and `/* */`, and NO REGULAR-EXPRESSION BRANCH. `sourceTokens()` at :168 already has one (`canStartRegularExpression` + `readRegularExpression`); the omission exists only in the template-expression scanner.

MECHANISM: walking `value.replace(/'/gu, ...)`, at the `/` of `/'/gu` the `next` char is `'`, so it is neither `//` nor `/*`; control falls to `else`, steps ONE char forward, and lands ON the quote inside the regex. The `'` branch then fires `readQuoted` from there, pairing that quote against the next `'` in the file (inside `"'\\''"`). Pairing stays off-by-one until a quote opens a run that hits end-of-line, where `readQuoted` (:92) throws `unterminated quoted source token`.

MINIMAL REPRO, no daemon involved:  const x = `${s.replace(/'/gu, "y")}`;
Any regex literal containing a quote character, inside a template expression.

THE SILENT HALF IS WORSE THAN THE RED: the scan `throw`s on the FIRST unreadable file, so one such file blinds the boundary check for EVERY file after it in walk order. This test is the fence keeping `@moe/scheduler` internals out of the rest of the tree; while it is red it is also not checking a scan-order tail of the repo at all.

SCOPE: test-only, one function, one file. Restores coverage rather than adding it. Filed by an idle worker seat with no claimed row; the chat escalation (msg-67929259, chan-ced99359) returned `routingTargets: []` because the channel Loop Guard had already capped, so it notified nobody — this row is the escalation. Reported unowned by qa-2702df88 as the board's only reproducible red.
definitionOfDone: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts` is EXIT 0 with all cases passing, quoted with its real output, and `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-environment.ts` is UNCHANGED by this row — the daemon file is correct TypeScript and editing it would hide the scanner defect rather than fix it.

`templateExpressionEnd()` consumes a regular-expression literal as ONE token, gated the same way `sourceTokens()` gates its own regex branch. State in a step note whether the gating helper was reused or duplicated, and if duplicated, why.

A regression case asserts the minimal shape directly — a regex literal containing a quote character inside a `${...}` — alongside the existing table at :264. Assert on the SCANNER's result for that source text, not on the daemon file, so the arm survives that file changing or moving.

AN ARM PROVES THE SCAN DOES NOT SILENTLY STOP EARLY. The current failure mode hides every file after the first unreadable one; a fix that only removes the throw would leave that hole open. Assert the scan reaches a known-last file, or that the count of files scanned equals the count enumerated.

Confirm by measurement whether the blinded tail contained any real boundary violation that was being hidden: run the fixed scan and report the number of files now scanned versus before, and name any violation it newly reports. If none, say so explicitly — a clean result here is a finding, not an absence.
No net new production code. The whole change is inside `packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts`.

implementationPlan.description: Capture the pre-change baseline and protect scope. Record the task merge-base/HEAD and git status --porcelain for the owned test and apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-environment.ts; hash the latter and leave it untouched. Note foreign dirt without reverting/stashing/staging it. Before editing, preserve the live scanner bytes out of tree under a task-and-worker-specific name, run the task-comment baseline census against those bytes, and record enumerated/completed/attempted/unattempted counts, first failing path and violations before failure. Re-run the reported focused repro and pin its actual error. Capture the required repository-lane merge-base failure sets for step 5; never label a peer-dirty working-tree run as a clean merge-base baseline. If a failing input differs from the merge-base, obtain comparison bytes in a temporary git-archive snapshot (not a sibling worktree), without changing the shared checkout. DoD 1/5/6. No committed probes or evidence artifacts.

TDD (load test-driven-development): extend the existing allowed/forbidden tables around forbiddenImportCases and allowedContentCases with literal source strings containing a quote-bearing regex inside a template expression. Include the exact minimal shape const x = `${s.replace(/'/gu, "y")}`; and assert templateExpressionEnd returns the closing-brace index, NOT EOF (current measurement: expected 34, actual 37). An empty moduleSpecifiers result alone is already green before the fix and is not the regression. Pair the source with a following genuine forbidden import and add an import inside the same expression after the regex; assert exact moduleSpecifiers arrays and containsForbiddenSchedulerImport=true, with corresponding allowed regex/prose=false controls. Cover apostrophe/double quote, braces and slash inside a character class, escaped delimiter, flags, regex at expression start, line/block comments before a regex, nested templates/braces, and division after an identifier/number/closing parenthesis/string/template. Add a malformed-regex arm through the scanner asserting the exact existing lexical error 'unterminated regular expression source token', not merely threw. Keep case-generation/nonempty checks. Record red-first output for the closing-index and suffix-import regressions before implementing the matcher.

Fix templateExpressionEnd only for lexical recognition: reuse canStartRegularExpression and readRegularExpression after the existing comment branches so a regex literal is consumed atomically and its quotes/braces cannot affect template depth. Track the expression's preceding significant SourceToken context while advancing: skip whitespace/comments, consume full identifiers with identifierStart/identifierPart, retain string and punctuation classifications, and handle a nested literal template as a string or an interpolated template's terminal } as punctuation, matching sourceTokens' regex-gating context. Maintain brace depth only outside quoted/comment/template/regex tokens. Preserve existing lexical failures; no catch-and-ignore, unconditional slash-as-regex, eager prefix re-tokenization, parser dependency, or change to daemon input. Reuse the helper and existing prefix sets rather than duplicating the gating policy; explain that choice in the step note and one concise inline why-comment. Avoid changing sourceTokens or broader unsupported-language semantics unless the named controls prove it necessary; report any additional scope need before taking another path. DoD 2/3/6.

Strengthen the existing real repository boundary arm without adding a second scanner. Enumerate sourceFiles for adapters, apps and packages into a complete ordered roster before scanning; preserve all existing exclusions, source extensions, sourceFiles ENOENT behavior and platform-native join/relative paths. Move each scanned-path append after successful contents classification, so an attempted-but-unreadable file is not counted as completed. Assert the nonempty successfully scanned path array equals the full independently enumerated relative-path array (therefore count and last-file coverage), retain scannedWitness and zero-violation assertions, and retain contextual fail-closed errors. Do not weaken the scan by swallowing an exception or skipping the failing daemon file. Emit a value-free run summary of enumerated/completed/violation counts, not source contents. The same delivered arm must provide DoD 4/5 evidence; a helper-only synthetic journey is insufficient. Compare with the pre-change census with explicit tree anchors and disclose roster drift. Report any newly exposed real boundary-violation paths; if none, say so explicitly only after the fixed real scan completes. Route any foreign violation to its owner rather than editing or excluding the input.

Concentrated verification. Verify the named regression fails with template regex handling disabled and that the real repository completeness assertion fails if its loop stops after the first completed file; assert the intended lexical-error/closing-index or path-count/roster mismatch, not an unrelated refusal. Prefer process-local transforms of this same test module. If an on-disk drill is necessary, first record exact-path git status and live SHA256, create a fresh out-of-tree backup whose name carries task id AND worker id, confirm backup hash against the live pre-mutation hash, and run no drill while a full-suite lease is active. Restore by copying that backup (never git restore/checkout), then in a SEPARATE call prove the restored live hash equals the recorded pre-mutation hash, including tracked/dirty/untracked paths. After all restores run foreground pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck and pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test, requiring nonzero Test Files/Tests counts. Run the required wider legs as separate foreground commands: pnpm typecheck; pnpm test; pnpm verify:foundation; pnpm verify:store; pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test; pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test. These semicolons list commands, not a shell chain: capture each real exit status independently, never pipe away pnpm's exit. Compare the wider failing-path sets at merge-base and final tree, disclose exact foreign failing lines/paths, and require no newly introduced owned-path failure plus green owned-package legs. Root pnpm test alone does not cover apps/**. Finish with the exact complete_task evidence command: pnpm exec vitest run packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts. Require EXIT 0, nonzero Test Files and Tests counts, and the real census summary; quote them verbatim with before/after counts and any newly exposed violation finding. Verify no row-owned diff to the daemon file and no production-source changes. Windows/macOS/Linux: native path APIs, standalone pnpm argv, no hard-coded pnpm.cmd Node launcher or bash-only chaining. DoD 1/4/5/6.

Final adversarial self-review (load adversarial-self-review): read the exact owned diff as a hostile reviewer. Check regex-versus-division context after whitespace/comments/strings/nested templates, escaped/class-contained braces and quotes, recursive nesting and malformed input, and ensure the regression does not pass via EOF swallowing. Verify the full-roster denominator is captured before the walk and completion is recorded only after classification; catch-and-ignore and loop truncation must not fabricate green. Confirm the recorded targeted red-first/drill evidence exercised those exact surfaces, restoration was proven, and both original boundary fences remain intact. Check concurrent shared-tree changes are disclosed, only the named test file is delivered, and no scratch/debug/probe/artifact or source-content logging was added. No docs/API/export changes are needed; keep explanatory comments in this file only. If review changes bytes, rerun step 5 rather than relying on prior output. Complete only with durable evidence/comment detail under truncation caps, report this path in modifiedFiles, and let the wrapper land the attributed commit for QA.
